title: Set-presheaf sheafification detects local bijectivity
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$ containing the objects and arrows of a small category $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $J$ be a Grothendieck topology on $\mathcal C$, specified by covering sieves: a sieve is a set of arrows with common target closed under precomposition; the maximal sieve covers, and covering sieves satisfy pullback stability and transitivity. Let $P,Q:\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{Set}_{\mathcal U}$ be presheaves and $v:P\to Q$ a natural transformation. Its associated-sheaf map $v^\#:P^\#\to Q^\#$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] is an isomorphism if and only if both of the following hold. For every $V\in\mathcal C$ and $q\in Q(V)$, there is a covering sieve $S$ on $V$ such that for each $u:W\to V$ in $S$ there is $p_u\in P(W)$ with $v_W(p_u)=u^*q$. For every $V\in\mathcal C$ and $p,p'\in P(V)$ with $v_V(p)=v_V(p')$, there is a covering sieve $S$ on $V$ such that $u^*p=u^*p'$ for each $u:W\to V$ in $S$. No fibre products in $\mathcal C$ or subcanonical hypothesis are assumed.

from.place: Proof opening 'Choose a compactification c=(j,p)' of thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale: arbitrary-site descent foundation for the affine-local compactification repair; in the descendant boundary-lifting proof, the local acyclic fibration square is solved after hypercover refinement before the mapping-space descent argument (DHI Proposition 5.1). Supporting input: Dugger--Hollander--Isaksen Proposition 3.2 and equation (3.4), v2 HTML lines 293-339. Homotopy-sheaf input before strictification: DHI Proposition 3.1, or Dugger--Isaksen Theorem 6.15(a), applied to a boundary square. Precisely the passage from associated homotopy-sheaf isomorphisms to local representatives and equality, before the relative boundary lift.
